clue.text: Manoeuvring of vehicle makes pet run riot, then collapse

indicators.note: to collapse is to fall into a heap, so the four words before it are knocked down and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A pet running riot and then collapsing in a heap, oddly linked to a driving move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' looks like the anagram signal for 'pet run', but it is fodder too: the signal is 'collapse', acting on PET RUN RIOT THEN together. 'makes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the standard driving-test manoeuvre for turning a car round in a narrow road using forward, reverse and forward moves.

clue.text: See best standing on head

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word standing on its head is upside down, so the word for best is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the tops is the best, as in 'she's the tops'

explanation.surface: An instruction to look at whoever is best at doing a headstand.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Within a part of India lurks unknown artist

indicators.note: the unknown is placed within the Indian state's name
something that lurks hides inside, so the unknown sits inside the state's name

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, here Y

explanation.surface: An unknown painter hiding away somewhere in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Francisco Goya was the great Spanish painter of the late 18th and early 19th centuries.

clue.text: Scheme to set bar up in secluded seaside location

indicators.note: the reversed pub word goes in the bay word

parts.note: a cove is a small sheltered bay on the coast

indicators.note: together with 'up' this tells us to set the word for bar upwards, so it is read backwards in a down light
in a down clue 'up' means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an inn is a pub, a place with a bar

explanation.surface: A plan to put up a bar in a quiet cove by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light, 'set ... up' means the pub word is read from the bottom upwards. 'bar' looks like an obstacle, but here it stands for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To connive is to plot or conspire secretly, so it is a verb synonym of scheme.

clue.text: Belts with ammunition stop soldier moving

parts.note: to ban something is to stop or prohibit it

indicators.note: moving the letters of the following word around rearranges them

explanation.surface: Ammunition belts that halt a soldier in his tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandoliers are shoulder belts with pockets or loops for carrying cartridges.

clue.text: Sue being agile, catching one pet?

indicators.note: the agile word catches, that is holds inside it, the other pieces

parts.note: supple means flexible or agile
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cat is a common household pet

explanation.surface: Someone called Sue is nimble enough to catch a pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a name, but it is the verb: to beg or petition. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue can mean to plead or petition, and to supplicate is to beg humbly.

clue.text: More than one wild animal in river by vessel delights

parts.note: in means fashionable, as does hip
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
a pot is a cooking vessel
amuses means entertains or delights

explanation.surface: A wild animal in a river beside a boat gives pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but is a piece: in = HIP, fashionable. 'by' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippos are large wild African mammals, and the plural form fits 'more than one'.

clue.text: Laundress might need to shift gloopy yellow stuff

indicators.note: to shift the letters is to move them about into a new order

explanation.surface: A laundress may have to remove a sticky yellow stain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like the laundress's work (or a dress) but rearranges LAUNDRESS MIGHT. 'need to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the hot, bright yellow condiment served with roast beef, thick and gloopy in the jar.

clue.text: Sober and at ease, consuming water

indicators.note: the word for at ease swallows the water word, holding it inside

parts.note: rested means relaxed or at ease
rain is water falling from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone sober and relaxed, drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained means calm and moderate, much like sober in its sense of serious and unshowy.

clue.text: Go off hill after climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means going upwards, so the hill word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: Setting out after climbing a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay, and food that goes off has begun to decay.

clue.text: Quiet time to get something to read?

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A spell of quiet time to settle down with a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheet of a book is a page, a thing you read; the question mark flags the loose description.

clue.text: What fuels boiler?

indicators.note: the letters that fuel the word boiler, sitting at its centre, give the hidden piece

explanation.surface: A simple question about what a heating boiler runs on.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition, and the answer also sits inside 'boiler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Many domestic boilers burn heating oil as their fuel.

clue.text: What you see in cycle velodrome at different heights

parts.words: What you see in cycle velodrome
parts.note: in the two words 'cycle velodrome' the word level is visible but broken across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A view of a cycle track whose banking rises and falls.
explanation.walkthrough: cycLE VELodrome holds LEVEL, split between two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A split-level house or floor has parts at different heights, a few steps apart.

clue.text: Bury run, leader in race being unwelcome visitor

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
to lope is to run with a long easy stride

indicators.note: the leader of the word race is its first letter

explanation.surface: A burial, a run and a race leader, all oddly linked to an intruder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the English town but is the verb. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An interloper is an intruder who pushes in where they are not wanted.

clue.text: Member getting very friendly with name not provided is recognised

parts.note: a leg is a limb, which is a member of the body

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is not supplied, so it is dropped from the friendly word

parts.note: intimate means very close or friendly

explanation.surface: A club member getting close to someone whose name is withheld is acknowledged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'with' join, and 'is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful or accepted as valid, which is to say officially recognised.

clue.text: Girl, one facing endless peril

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: without its end means the last letter of the peril word is removed

parts.note: a risk is a danger or peril

explanation.surface: A girl alone, facing danger that never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a girl's name, as crossword setters often use 'girl' for a female first name.

clue.text: Six books in a set sitting beside mature wine

indicators.note: the pieces sit side by side, one beside the next

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral for six
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
to age is to mature, as wine and cheese do

explanation.surface: Six books placed in a set alongside a bottle of mature wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a set' is a link phrase: the New Testament is the set of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintage is a wine from a particular year's harvest, especially one of high quality.

clue.text: These played harps, but not the harp-playing types!

indicators.note: the letters of these and harps are played with, rearranged into new order
the letters of the word 'the' are not part of the result and are taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: These people played harps, yet aren't the sort known for harp playing!
explanation.walkthrough: Pool THESE and HARPS, remove the letters of THE ('but not'), and the 'played' letters SEHARPS rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels of the highest order, traditionally pictured in heaven playing harps.

clue.text: Fellow hiding love is a bit more wet

indicators.note: the fellow word hides the love letter inside it

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man or fellow
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man concealing his love is slightly damper.
explanation.definitionFit: Moist means slightly wet, so its comparative form means a little wetter.

clue.text: Celebrity that's knocked over by despicable people

indicators.note: something knocked over is turned the other way round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: rats are contemptible or treacherous people

explanation.surface: A celebrity floored by some nasty characters.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a famous performer, a celebrity.

clue.text: Household collections famous Frenchman featured in odd bits of text

indicators.note: the Frenchman's name features inside the two selected letters
the odd-numbered letters, first and third, of the word text

parts.note: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, the philosopher of the Enlightenment

explanation.surface: A famous Frenchman appearing in scraps of writing about household goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of text' gives T and X, which go round ROUSSEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is a bride's collection of clothes and household linen for married life.

clue.text: Son meeting father in spring

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A son meets his father in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' joins the pieces and 'in' links to the definition: a spring, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a mineral spring, or a resort built around one.

clue.text: Garland from the French island

parts.note: le is the masculine form of 'the' in French

explanation.surface: A garland brought from a French island.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn round the neck.

clue.text: After first half of month perform in sport

indicators.note: the first half of the month's name is its opening two letters

parts.note: June is a month of the year
to do is to carry out or perform

explanation.surface: Taking part in a sport once the middle of the month arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Judo is a Japanese martial art practised as an Olympic sport.

clue.text: Greek character thus transformed Italy, showing ability to bring harmony?

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as written

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so the country's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek figure changing Italy by bringing it harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicality is musical talent, including a feel for harmony; the question mark marks the playful sense.

clue.text: Heartless trick will make you gossip

indicators.note: without its heart means the central letter of the trick word is taken out

parts.note: to cheat is to trick or deceive

explanation.surface: A cruel trick that will set people talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally, much like gossiping.

clue.text: Writer that one associates with a certain Mary

definitions.meaning: Charles ... was an English essayist, author of the Essays of Elia

definitions.text: that one associates with a certain Mary
definitions.meaning: the nursery rhyme says Mary had a little one with fleece white as snow; also Mary was the writer's sister

explanation.surface: A writer you link with a particular Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb the essayist co-wrote Tales from Shakespeare with his sister Mary, and the rhyme's Mary had a young sheep.

clue.text: A lot may be about to be getting a hit from above?

definitions.text: A lot may be about to be
definitions.meaning: an auction lot is about to be sold when the auctioneer's gavel is raised
taken literally, something struck from above sits beneath a striking tool

explanation.surface: Something that may be about to take a blow from overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means up for sale at auction, where the gavel falls to close each sale.
